functions.name: agile_scores_all
functions.description: A score table for every candidate who has completed level 2, the Agile Compatibility Index: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, the Commitment / Focus / Openness / Respect / Courage breakdown, the total out of the level maximum, the compatibility band that total falls in, the sincerity class, and when it was completed. Highest total first. Can be narrowed to one program.
whenToUse: give me all the level 2 scores
ACI scores for everyone who completed it
agile compatibility results as a table
whenNotToUse: Not for level 1 — that is behavioural_scores_all.
Not for one candidate — that is candidate_agile_index.

program.description: Optional program name to narrow to, full or partial — for example "College Students".

functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH lvl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, max_score FROM assessment_levels WHERE level_number = 2 ORDER BY id
), att AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.registration_id)
         a.id AS attempt_id, a.registration_id, a.assessment_session_id,
         a.total_score, a.max_score_snapshot, a.sincerity_class, a.completed_at,
         lvl.max_score AS level_max
    FROM assessment_attempts a
    JOIN lvl ON lvl.id = a.assessment_level_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND a.status = 'COMPLETED'
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY a.registration_id, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC
)
SELECT att.registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.agile->>'Commitment')::numeric AS commitment,
       (ar.agile->>'Focus')::numeric AS focus,
       (ar.agile->>'Openness')::numeric AS openness,
       (ar.agile->>'Respect')::numeric AS respect,
       (ar.agile->>'Courage')::numeric AS courage,
       att.total_score AS total,
       coalesce(nullif(att.max_score_snapshot, 0), att.level_max) AS out_of,
       coalesce(b.level_name, 'outside the published band range') AS band,
       b.compatibility_tag AS band_summary,
       att.sincerity_class,
       att.completed_at,
       (ar.report_number IS NOT NULL) AS report_ready
  FROM att
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = att.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.report_number, x.agile_scores AS agile
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = att.assessment_session_id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.program_id FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.id = att.assessment_session_id ORDER BY s2.id LIMIT 1) sp ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(sp.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.level_name, x.compatibility_tag
         FROM aci_score_bands x
        WHERE x.is_active AND x.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
          AND att.total_score BETWEEN x.min_score AND x.max_score
        ORDER BY x.display_order, x.id
        LIMIT 1) b ON TRUE
 WHERE (cast({{param:program}} AS text) IS NULL OR p.name ILIKE '%' || {{param:program}} || '%')
 ORDER BY att.total_score DESC NULLS LAST, r.full_name

functions.name: attempts_expiring_soon
functions.description: Candidates in your company whose current assessment level has a deadline coming up and is not finished, soonest first, with how many hours are left. Use this to chase people before they run out of time.
whenToUse: who is about to run out of time
which assessments expire this week
who should I chase
anything expiring in the next 48 hours
whenNotToUse: Not for deadlines that have already passed — that is stalled_attempts.
Not for one candidate — use candidate_level_scores.

within_hours.description: How far ahead to look, in hours. Defaults to 72 (three days).

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       a.status,
       coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) AS deadline,
       round(extract(epoch FROM coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) - now()) / 3600) AS hours_left
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND a.status IN ('NOT_STARTED', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'PARTIALLY_EXPIRED')
   AND coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at)
       BETWEEN now() AND now() + make_interval(hours => coalesce({{param:within_hours}}::int, 72))
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY a.id, deadline

functions.name: behavioural_scores_all
functions.description: A score table for every candidate who has completed level 1, the behavioural (DISC) assessment: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, the Dominance / Influence / Steadiness / Compliance breakdown, the total out of the level maximum, the trait code and blended style, the sincerity reading, and when it was completed. Highest total first. Can be narrowed to one trait code or one program. Candidates whose report has not been generated still appear, with a total but no D/I/S/C breakdown.
whenToUse: give me all the scores of students who completed level 1
export the behavioural exam scores
DISC scores for everyone
list level 1 results as a table
whenNotToUse: Not for level 2 — that is agile_scores_all.
Not for one candidate — that is candidate_behavioural_profile.
Not for a count per trait code — that is trait_code_distribution.

program.description: Optional program name to narrow to, full or partial — for example "College Students".

trait_code.description: Optional two-letter behavioural trait code to narrow to, for example "DI", "CD" or "CS".

functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH lvl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, max_score FROM assessment_levels WHERE level_number = 1 ORDER BY id
), att AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.registration_id)
         a.id AS attempt_id, a.registration_id, a.assessment_session_id,
         a.total_score, a.max_score_snapshot, a.sincerity_index, a.sincerity_class,
         a.dominant_trait_id, a.completed_at, lvl.max_score AS level_max
    FROM assessment_attempts a
    JOIN lvl ON lvl.id = a.assessment_level_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND a.status = 'COMPLETED'
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY a.registration_id, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC
)
SELECT att.registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.disc->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
       (ar.disc->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
       (ar.disc->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
       (ar.disc->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
       att.total_score AS total,
       coalesce(nullif(att.max_score_snapshot, 0), att.level_max) AS out_of,
       pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       att.sincerity_index AS sincerity,
       att.sincerity_class,
       att.completed_at,
       (ar.report_number IS NOT NULL) AS report_ready
  FROM att
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = att.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.report_number, x.disc_scores AS disc
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = att.assessment_session_id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.program_id FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.id = att.assessment_session_id ORDER BY s2.id LIMIT 1) sp ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(sp.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = att.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE (cast({{param:trait_code}} AS text) IS NULL OR upper(pt.code) = upper({{param:trait_code}}))
   AND (cast({{param:program}} AS text) IS NULL OR p.name ILIKE '%' || {{param:program}} || '%')
 ORDER BY att.total_score DESC NULLS LAST, r.full_name

functions.name: candidate_agile_index
functions.description: One candidate's level 2 Agile Compatibility Index — Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect and Courage with the total, and which band the total falls in with its interpretation. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: what is this candidate's agile score
which ACI band is <candidate> in
how did they score on openness and courage
whenNotToUse: Not for the DISC letters — that is candidate_behavioural_profile.
Not for every level at once — that is candidate_level_scores.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Commitment')::numeric AS commitment,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Focus')::numeric      AS focus,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Openness')::numeric   AS openness,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Respect')::numeric    AS respect,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Courage')::numeric    AS courage,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric      AS total,
       b.level_name AS band,
       b.compatibility_tag AS band_summary,
       b.interpretation AS what_the_band_means,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN aci_score_bands b
         ON b.is_active AND b.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
        AND (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric BETWEEN b.min_score AND b.max_score
 WHERE ar.agile_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.agile_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND s.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_behavioural_profile
functions.description: One candidate's level 1 behavioural breakdown — Dominance, Influence, Steadiness and Compliance with the total, and the blended style those produce with what it means. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: what is this candidate's DISC profile
what personality style did <candidate> get
show me the behavioural breakdown for <candidate>
whenNotToUse: Not for the agile values — that is candidate_agile_index.
Not for every level at once — that is candidate_level_scores.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS total,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       pt.blended_style_desc AS what_the_style_means,
       ar.overall_sincerity,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE ar.disc_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.disc_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND s.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_iat_patterns
functions.description: One candidate's level 3 association-test result, one row per comparison: how much longer they took on one pairing than the other, whether that hesitation was low, moderate or strong, the error rate, and which pairing was slower. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: what did level 3 show for this candidate
where did <candidate> hesitate
show me the association patterns for <candidate>
whenNotToUse: Level 3 produces no numeric score — for scores use candidate_level_scores.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (m.module_order, im.id)
       im.display_name AS comparison,
       m.pattern_label AS hesitation,
       round(m.speed_gap_ms) AS hesitation_ms,
       round(m.compatible_average_ms) AS faster_pairing_ms,
       round(m.incompatible_average_ms) AS slower_pairing_ms,
       round(m.error_rate, 1) AS error_percent,
       im.slowed_on_description AS slower_pairing_was,
       m.status,
       m.completed_at
  FROM iat_attempt_modules m
  JOIN iat_modules im ON im.id = m.module_id
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = m.registration_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND m.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY m.module_order, im.id, m.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_iat_report
functions.description: One candidate's level 3 IAT report as it is stored: one row per bias area with the pattern strength found, the hesitation gap in milliseconds and the error rate, plus the written narrative of the report. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Level 3 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me the IAT report for <candidate>
what did the level 3 report say
read the bias report for this candidate
whenNotToUse: Not for the raw per-module timing data — that is candidate_iat_patterns.
Not for level 4 — that is candidate_metaphor_report.
Not for whether it exists at all — that is candidate_report_status.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (bias.ord)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       i.generated_at,
       bias.value->>'name' AS bias_area,
       bias.value->>'pattern' AS pattern_strength,
       round((bias.value->>'speedGapMs')::numeric) AS hesitation_ms,
       round((bias.value->>'errorRate')::numeric, 1) AS error_percent,
       i.report_text AS narrative
  FROM iat_reports i
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = i.registration_id
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(i.bias_map, '[]'::jsonb)) WITH ORDINALITY AS bias(value, ord)
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND i.status = 'DONE'
   AND i.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY bias.ord, i.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_level_scores
functions.description: One candidate's result at every assessment level, one row per level in order — the level name, what it measures, status, score out of the maximum with a percentage, and when it was finished. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Only returns candidates in your own company.
whenToUse: what were Priya's scores
how did this candidate do in each level
show me the level breakdown for <candidate>
what did they get for level 1
whenNotToUse: Not for finding the candidate in the first place — use find_candidate, then this.
Not for the D/I/S/C or agile detail — those are candidate_behavioural_profile.
Not for a whole cohort — use level_completion_funnel.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate. Ask for the candidate by name first if you do not have it.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (l.sort_order)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       a.status,
       a.total_score AS score,
       nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0) AS out_of,
       round(100.0 * a.total_score
             / nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0), 1) AS percent,
       a.sincerity_class,
       pt.blended_style_name AS dominant_style,
       a.started_at,
       a.completed_at
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = a.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND a.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY l.sort_order, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_metaphor_report
functions.description: One candidate's level 4 Metaphor report as it is stored: the written report and when it was generated. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Level 4 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me the metaphor report for <candidate>
what did the level 4 report say
whenNotToUse: Not for level 3 — that is candidate_iat_report.
Not for whether it exists at all — that is candidate_report_status.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (mr.assessment_attempt_id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       mr.generated_at,
       mr.markdown AS report
  FROM metaphor_reports mr
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = mr.registration_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND mr.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY mr.assessment_attempt_id DESC, mr.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, mr.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_report_status
functions.description: Whether one candidate's reports actually exist, checked against the stored report records rather than a status flag. Returns, per assessment session: the report number, whether the main report is generated and downloadable, when it was generated, the behavioural trait code and style it produced, and separately whether the level 3 IAT report and the level 4 Metaphor report exist. Takes a registration id from find_candidate.
whenToUse: is <candidate>'s report ready
can I see <candidate>'s report
has the report been generated for this candidate
does this candidate have an IAT or Metaphor report
whenNotToUse: Not for producing a download link — that is generate_candidate_report.
Not for the scores themselves — use candidate_behavioural_profile, candidate_agile_index, candidate_iat_report or candidate_metaphor_report.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       s.id AS session_id,
       s.status AS session_status,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.session_id IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_ready,
       (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_downloadable,
       ar.generated_at AS main_report_generated_at,
       pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       (iat.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS iat_report_ready,
       iat.generated_at AS iat_report_generated_at,
       (mr.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       mr.generated_at AS metaphor_report_generated_at,
       CASE
         WHEN ar.session_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Report is ready'
         WHEN s.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN 'Assessment finished, report not generated yet'
         ELSE 'No report — the assessment is ' || lower(coalesce(s.status, 'not started'))
       END AS readiness
  FROM registrations r
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_session_id AS session_id, x.report_number, x.report_url,
              x.generated_at, x.dominant_trait_id
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id, x.generated_at
         FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE'
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id, x.generated_at
         FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) mr ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND r.id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY s.id DESC

functions.name: candidate_status_counts
functions.description: Count your company's candidates grouped by the status of their latest assessment session (COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, EXPIRED, NOT_STARTED, and so on). Use this for "how many" questions rather than listing people.
whenToUse: how many candidates have completed the assessment
give me a breakdown of our candidates by status
how many are still pending
whenNotToUse: Not for the actual names — use list_candidates.
Not for one person — use find_candidate.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       count(DISTINCT r.id) AS candidates
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 GROUP BY coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION')
 ORDER BY candidates DESC

functions.name: candidates_by_trait_code
functions.description: The candidates whose behavioural result is one particular trait code — the two-letter DISC blend such as DI, CD or CS — as a table: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, the style that code means, the D / I / S / C breakdown and the total. Highest total first. Answers "list the DI trait code students".
whenToUse: list the students with the DI trait code
who are the Charismatic Leaders
show me everyone in the CD trait
whenNotToUse: Not for the counts per code — that is trait_code_distribution.
Not for every code at once — that is behavioural_scores_all.

trait_code.description: The behavioural trait code, one or two letters — for example "DI", "CD", "CS" or "C".

functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
         r.id AS registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
         coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program, ar.report_number,
         ar.dominant_trait_id,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS total,
         ar.generated_at
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
    LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
   WHERE ar.dominant_trait_id IS NOT NULL
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, ar.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, ar.id DESC
)
SELECT l.registration_id, l.candidate, l.user_id, l.program, l.report_number,
       pt.code AS trait_code, pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       l.dominance, l.influence, l.steadiness, l.compliance, l.total, l.generated_at
  FROM latest l
  JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = l.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE upper(pt.code) = upper({{param:trait_code}})
 ORDER BY l.total DESC NULLS LAST, l.candidate

functions.name: candidates_with_reports
functions.description: Every candidate who has a generated report, newest first, as a table: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, whether it is downloadable, their behavioural and agile totals, their trait code and style, and whether the level 3 IAT and level 4 Metaphor reports also exist. Optionally narrowed to one program.
whenToUse: show me the candidates who have reports
list the reports that are ready
give me report details for the ones who completed
which candidates can I download a report for
whenNotToUse: Not for one named candidate — use find_candidate then candidate_report_status.
Not for candidates without a report — that is list_candidates.

program.description: Optional program name to narrow to, full or partial — for example "College Students".

functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
         r.id AS registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
         coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program, s.id AS session_id,
         ar.report_number, ar.generated_at, ar.dominant_trait_id,
         (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS downloadable,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS behavioural_total,
         (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric AS agile_total
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
    LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND (cast({{param:program}} AS text) IS NULL OR p.name ILIKE '%' || {{param:program}} || '%')
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, ar.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, ar.id DESC
)
SELECT l.registration_id, l.candidate, l.user_id, l.program, l.report_number,
       l.downloadable, l.behavioural_total, l.agile_total,
       pt.code AS trait_code, pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM iat_reports i
                WHERE i.assessment_session_id = l.session_id AND i.status = 'DONE') AS iat_report_ready,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM metaphor_reports mr
                WHERE mr.assessment_session_id = l.session_id) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       l.generated_at
  FROM latest l
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = l.dominant_trait_id
 ORDER BY l.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, l.candidate

functions.name: corporate_credit_balance
functions.description: Show your company's assessment credit balance: how many credits are available now, how many were purchased in total, and whether the account is active.
whenToUse: how many credits do we have left
what is our credit balance
is our account active
whenNotToUse: Not for candidates or assessments — this is only the credit balance.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ca.id)
       ca.id,
       ca.company_name,
       ca.available_credits,
       ca.total_credits,
       ca.is_active
  FROM corporate_accounts ca
 WHERE {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ca.id

functions.name: corporate_credit_history
functions.description: Your company's assessment credit movements, most recent first: whether each entry added (CREDIT) or used (DEBIT) credits, how many, the reason, and the amount and payment status where one applies. Use this for "where did our credits go"; for the number remaining use corporate_credit_balance.
whenToUse: where did our credits go
show me our credit history
when did we last buy credits
what have we spent credits on
whenNotToUse: Not for the current balance — that is corporate_credit_balance.
Not for candidates — use list_candidates.

entry_type.description: Restrict to credits added or credits used. Leave unset for both.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (cl.id)
       cl.created_at AS entry_date,
       cl.ledger_type AS entry_type,
       cl.credit_delta AS credits,
       cl.reason,
       cl.per_credit_cost,
       cl.total_amount,
       cl.payment_status,
       cl.paid_on
  FROM corporate_credit_ledger cl
 WHERE (cast({{param:entry_type}} AS text) IS NULL OR cl.ledger_type = {{param:entry_type}})
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY cl.id DESC

functions.name: demo
functions.description: Lists the database tables this assistant is able to read, with the schema each one belongs to and an estimated row count. Optionally filters to tables whose name contains a given word. Use it to find out what data is available, or to check whether a particular table exists and has rows in it.
whenToUse: what tables are in the database
what data can you see
is there a table about orders
how many tables are there
which tables have data in them
whenNotToUse: Reading the contents of a table — this returns table names, never rows from them.

hideSchema.description: Schema to leave out of the results. Defaults to the assistant's own bookkeeping schema.

nameContains.description: Only list tables whose name contains this text. Leave out to list all of them.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT n.nspname                                   AS schema_name,
       c.relname                                   AS table_name,
       CASE WHEN c.reltuples < 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE round(c.reltuples)::bigint END    AS estimated_rows,
       CASE WHEN c.reltuples < 0 THEN 'never analysed'
            WHEN c.reltuples = 0 THEN 'empty'
            ELSE round(c.reltuples)::bigint || ' rows (estimated)'
       END                                         AS row_summary
  FROM pg_class c
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
 WHERE c.relkind IN ('r', 'p')
   AND n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
   AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%'
   AND n.nspname <> COALESCE({{param:hideSchema}}, '')
   AND has_table_privilege(c.oid, 'SELECT')
   AND (COALESCE({{param:nameContains}}, '') = ''
        OR c.relname ILIKE '%' || {{param:nameContains}} || '%')
 ORDER BY n.nspname, c.relname

functions.name: find_candidate
functions.description: Find one candidate (a registered person) within your company by their name, and return the identifiers other functions need: their registration id, their user id, the program they are on, the status of their latest assessment session, and whether their main, IAT and Metaphor reports have actually been generated. When several people match the name it returns them as choices rather than picking one.
whenToUse: find the candidate called <name>
look up <name>
which registration is <name>
whenNotToUse: Not for a list of everyone — that is list_candidates.
Not for a platform user by email — that is find_user.

name.description: The candidate's name, full or partial.

registration_id.description: The registration id, if it is already known.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id AS id,
       r.full_name AS label,
       coalesce(p.name, 'no program') || ' · ' || coalesce(s.status, 'no session yet')
         || ' · ' || CASE WHEN ar.n > 0 THEN 'report ready' ELSE 'no report' END AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN r.id = {{param:registration_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(r.full_name) = lower({{param:name}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       r.full_name,
       r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       r.status AS registration_status,
       coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       (ar.n > 0) AS report_ready,
       (iat.n > 0) AS iat_report_ready,
       (mr.n > 0) AS metaphor_report_ready
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.id, s2.status, s2.program_id
         FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.registration_id = r.id
        ORDER BY s2.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s2.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) s ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE') iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) mr ON TRUE
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND (
        r.full_name ILIKE '%' || {{param:name}} || '%'
     OR r.id = {{param:registration_id}}
   )
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id

functions.name: find_corporate_account
functions.description: Administrator lookup of a corporate (company) account by company name, returning its credit balance and whether it is active. When several companies match, the agent asks which one.
whenToUse: look up the corporate account for Touchmark
how many credits does <company> have
find company <name>
whenNotToUse: Not for a candidate or a person — use find_user or find_candidate.
Available to administrators only.

company_name.description: Full or partial company name, e.g. "Touchmark".

corporate_account_id.description: The corporate account id. Set only when resolving which company was meant after the agent asked.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ca.id)
       ca.id AS id,
       ca.company_name AS label,
       ca.available_credits::text || ' of ' || ca.total_credits::text || ' credits left' AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN ca.id = {{param:corporate_account_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(ca.company_name) = lower({{param:company_name}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       ca.company_name,
       ca.available_credits,
       ca.total_credits,
       ca.is_active
  FROM corporate_accounts ca
 WHERE ca.company_name ILIKE '%' || {{param:company_name}} || '%'
    OR ca.id = {{param:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY ca.id

functions.name: find_user
functions.description: Administrator lookup of a platform user by email address, returning their role (STUDENT, CORPORATE, AFFILIATE, ADMIN) and whether the account is active or blocked. When several emails match a partial search, the agent asks which one.
whenToUse: find the user with email jane@example.com
is the account for <email> blocked
what role does <email> have
whenNotToUse: Not for a candidate's assessment progress — use find_candidate.
Available to administrators only.

user_id.description: The user id. Set only when resolving which user was meant after the agent asked.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (u.id)
       u.id AS id,
       u.email AS label,
       u.role || ' · ' || CASE WHEN u.is_blocked THEN 'blocked' WHEN u.is_active THEN 'active' ELSE 'inactive' END AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN u.id = {{param:user_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(u.email) = lower({{param:email}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       u.email,
       u.role,
       u.is_active,
       u.is_blocked,
       u.corporate_id
  FROM users u
 WHERE u.email ILIKE '%' || {{param:email}} || '%'
    OR u.id = {{param:user_id}}
 ORDER BY u.id

functions.name: generate_candidate_report
functions.description: Prepare a candidate's assessment report and hand back a download link. Takes the candidate's user id, which find_candidate returns — look the person up by name first. The report is rendered in the background and the link arrives when it is ready. Only candidates in your own company can be generated for.
whenToUse: download the report for Priya Sharma
generate a report for this candidate
get me <candidate>'s report
send me the report for <candidate>
whenNotToUse: Not for checking whether a report is ready — find_candidate already says so.
Not for a whole cohort at once.
Look the candidate up by name first; this takes the id that lookup returns.

user_id.description: The candidate's user id, as returned by find_candidate. Never guess this — look the candidate up by name first.

report_type.description: Which report to produce. Leave unset for the standard full report.

precondition.denyMessage: That candidate is not in your account.
precondition.sqlTemplate: SELECT 1 FROM registrations r WHERE r.user_id = {{param:user_id}} AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}

functions.name: generate_my_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: prepare their assessment report and hand back a download link. Takes a little while — the report is rendered in the background and the link arrives when it is ready. Only ever produces the caller's own report.
whenToUse: download my report
send me my report
can I get a copy of my assessment report
generate my report
whenNotToUse: Not for checking whether a report already exists — that is my_report.
Not for scores — those are my_level_scores.
Only ever produces the caller's own report.

report_type.description: Which report to produce. Leave unset for the standard full report.

precondition.denyMessage: I could not find a registration for you, so there is no report to prepare.
precondition.sqlTemplate: SELECT 1 FROM registrations r WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE AND {{scope:user_id}}

functions.name: level_completion_funnel
functions.description: How your company's candidates are distributed across the assessment levels: for each level reached, how many attempts are completed, in progress, not started or expired, how many distinct candidates it covers, and the average score of the completed ones. Shows where a cohort is stuck.
whenToUse: where are our candidates getting stuck
how many have finished each level
give me a level by level breakdown
what is the average score at level 2
whenNotToUse: Not for one candidate — use candidate_level_scores.
Not for overall session status — use candidate_status_counts.
A level no candidate has reached does not appear at all.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'COMPLETED')   AS completed,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'IN_PROGRESS') AS in_progress,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'NOT_STARTED') AS not_started,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) FILTER (WHERE a.status IN ('EXPIRED', 'PARTIALLY_EXPIRED')) AS expired,
       count(DISTINCT a.registration_id) AS candidates,
       round(avg(a.total_score) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'COMPLETED'), 1) AS average_score
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 GROUP BY l.level_number, l.name, l.pattern_type, l.sort_order
 ORDER BY l.sort_order

functions.name: level_report_coverage
functions.description: For each assessment level in order — level 1 Behavioural, level 2 ACI, level 3 IAT, level 4 Metaphor — how many attempts exist, how many are completed, how many reports have been generated, and which kind of report that level produces. Levels 3 and 4 keep their reports separately from the main report, and each is counted where it is actually stored.
whenToUse: how many reports exist per level
which levels are missing reports
level 3 and level 4 report coverage
whenNotToUse: Not for where candidates are stuck — that is level_completion_funnel.
Not for a single overall total — that is report_readiness_summary.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH att AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.id)
         a.id, a.assessment_level_id, a.status
    FROM assessment_attempts a
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY a.id
), lvl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, level_number, name, pattern_type, sort_order
    FROM assessment_levels ORDER BY id
), generated AS (
  SELECT 1 AS level_number, count(DISTINCT ar.assessment_session_id) AS n
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
   WHERE ar.disc_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.disc_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   UNION ALL
  SELECT 2, count(DISTINCT ar.assessment_session_id)
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
   WHERE ar.agile_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.agile_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   UNION ALL
  SELECT 3, count(DISTINCT i.id)
    FROM iat_reports i
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = i.registration_id
   WHERE i.status = 'DONE'
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   UNION ALL
  SELECT 4, count(DISTINCT mr.id)
    FROM metaphor_reports mr
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = mr.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
)
SELECT lvl.level_number,
       lvl.name AS level,
       lvl.pattern_type AS measures,
       count(DISTINCT att.id) AS attempts,
       count(DISTINCT att.id) FILTER (WHERE att.status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed,
       coalesce(max(generated.n), 0) AS reports_generated,
       CASE lvl.level_number
         WHEN 3 THEN 'IAT narrative report (iat_reports)'
         WHEN 4 THEN 'Metaphor narrative report (metaphor_reports)'
         WHEN 5 THEN 'no report defined for this level'
         ELSE 'Main assessment report (assessment_reports)'
       END AS report_kind
  FROM lvl
  LEFT JOIN att ON att.assessment_level_id = lvl.id
  LEFT JOIN generated ON generated.level_number = lvl.level_number
 GROUP BY lvl.level_number, lvl.name, lvl.pattern_type, lvl.sort_order
 ORDER BY lvl.sort_order

functions.name: list_candidates
functions.description: List the candidates registered under your company, each with their registration id, user id, program, the status of their latest assessment session, and whether their main, IAT and Metaphor reports have actually been generated. Optionally narrowed to one session status.
whenToUse: list our candidates
who is registered
show me everyone who has not started
whenNotToUse: Not for one named person — that is find_candidate.
Not for only those with reports — that is candidates_with_reports.

session_status.description: Optional session status to narrow to.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id,
       r.full_name,
       r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       (ar.n > 0) AS report_ready,
       (iat.n > 0) AS iat_report_ready,
       (mr.n > 0) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       r.created_at
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.id, s2.status, s2.program_id
         FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.registration_id = r.id
        ORDER BY s2.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s2.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) s ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE') iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) mr ON TRUE
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND (cast({{param:session_status}} AS text) IS NULL
        OR coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') = {{param:session_status}})
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id

functions.name: my_agile_index
functions.description: For the signed-in student: the level 2 Agile Compatibility Index — their Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect and Courage scores, the total, and which band that total falls in (Agile Naturalist, Adaptive, Learner or Resistant) with the interpretation of that band.
whenToUse: what is my agile score
what is my ACI
what band am I in
how did I do on commitment and courage
whenNotToUse: Not for the DISC letters — that is my_behavioural_profile.
Not for every level at once — that is my_level_scores.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Commitment')::numeric AS commitment,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Focus')::numeric      AS focus,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Openness')::numeric   AS openness,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Respect')::numeric    AS respect,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'Courage')::numeric    AS courage,
       (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric      AS total,
       b.level_name AS band,
       b.compatibility_tag AS band_summary,
       b.interpretation AS what_the_band_means,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  LEFT JOIN aci_score_bands b
         ON b.is_active AND b.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
        AND (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric BETWEEN b.min_score AND b.max_score
 WHERE ar.agile_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.agile_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: my_assessment_status
functions.description: For the signed-in student: the status of their own assessment session(s) — which program, whether it is completed, in progress or expired, and whether the report is ready. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenToUse: what is the status of my assessment
have I finished my assessment
is my assessment still in progress
whenNotToUse: Not for the report itself — use my_report.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id)
       s.id,
       r.full_name,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       s.status AS session_status,
       coalesce(s.is_report_ready, false) AS report_ready,
       s.completed_at,
       s.created_at
  FROM assessment_sessions s
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = s.program_id
  LEFT JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY s.id DESC

functions.name: my_behavioural_profile
functions.description: For the signed-in student: the level 1 behavioural breakdown — their Dominance, Influence, Steadiness and Compliance scores, the total, and the blended style those four produce (such as "Creative Thinker") with what that style means.
whenToUse: what is my DISC score
what is my personality style
what are my dominance and influence scores
explain my behavioural profile
whenNotToUse: Not for every level at once — that is my_level_scores.
Not for the agile values from level 2 — that is my_agile_index.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (ar.id)
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
       (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS total,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       pt.blended_style_desc AS what_the_style_means,
       ar.overall_sincerity,
       ar.generated_at
  FROM assessment_reports ar
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE ar.disc_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.disc_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY ar.id DESC

functions.name: my_iat_patterns
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their level 3 association-test result, one row per comparison. Each row gives how much longer they took on one pairing than the other, whether that hesitation was low, moderate or strong, their error rate, and which pairing was the slower one.
whenToUse: what did level 3 show
what were my IAT results
where did I hesitate
what are my association patterns
whenNotToUse: Level 3 has no numeric score, so this is not a "what did I get" answer — for scores use my_level_scores.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (m.module_order, im.id)
       im.display_name AS comparison,
       m.pattern_label AS hesitation,
       round(m.speed_gap_ms) AS hesitation_ms,
       round(m.compatible_average_ms) AS faster_pairing_ms,
       round(m.incompatible_average_ms) AS slower_pairing_ms,
       round(m.error_rate, 1) AS error_percent,
       im.slowed_on_description AS slower_pairing_was,
       m.status,
       m.completed_at
  FROM iat_attempt_modules m
  JOIN iat_modules im ON im.id = m.module_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY m.module_order, im.id, m.id DESC

functions.name: my_iat_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own level 3 IAT report as it is stored — one row per bias area with the pattern strength, the hesitation gap in milliseconds and the error rate, plus the written narrative. Level 3 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me my IAT report
what did my level 3 report say
read my bias report
whenNotToUse: Not for the raw per-module timing data — that is my_iat_patterns.
Not for level 4 — that is my_metaphor_report.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (bias.ord)
       i.generated_at,
       bias.value->>'name' AS bias_area,
       bias.value->>'pattern' AS pattern_strength,
       round((bias.value->>'speedGapMs')::numeric) AS hesitation_ms,
       round((bias.value->>'errorRate')::numeric, 1) AS error_percent,
       i.report_text AS narrative
  FROM iat_reports i
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(i.bias_map, '[]'::jsonb)) WITH ORDINALITY AS bias(value, ord)
 WHERE i.status = 'DONE'
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY bias.ord, i.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC

functions.name: my_level_scores
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their result at every assessment level, one row per level in order — the level name, what it measures, whether it is completed, the score out of the maximum with a percentage, and when it was finished. Levels 1 and 2 carry a numeric score; levels 3 and 4 are pattern-based and show completion rather than a mark.
whenToUse: what are my scores
how did I do in each level
what did I get for level 2
show me my assessment results
which levels have I finished
whenNotToUse: Not for the D/I/S/C breakdown of level 1 — that is my_behavioural_profile.
Not for the five agile values behind the level 2 total — that is my_agile_index.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (l.sort_order)
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       a.status,
       a.total_score AS score,
       nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0) AS out_of,
       round(100.0 * a.total_score
             / nullif(coalesce(nullif(a.max_score_snapshot, 0), l.max_score), 0), 1) AS percent,
       a.sincerity_class,
       pt.blended_style_name AS dominant_style,
       a.started_at,
       a.completed_at
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = a.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY l.sort_order, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC

functions.name: my_metaphor_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own level 4 Metaphor report as it is stored — the written report and when it was generated. Level 4 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me my metaphor report
what did my level 4 report say
whenNotToUse: Not for level 3 — that is my_iat_report.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (mr.assessment_attempt_id)
       mr.generated_at,
       mr.markdown AS report
  FROM metaphor_reports mr
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY mr.assessment_attempt_id DESC, mr.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, mr.id DESC

functions.name: my_registration_status
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own registration details — their name, the program they registered for, the registration status, payment status, and whether AI counsellor access is enabled. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenToUse: what is my name
what did I register for
what is my registration status
do I have AI counsellor access
what are my details
whenNotToUse: Not for assessment progress or reports — use my_assessment_status or my_report.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id,
       r.full_name,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       r.status AS registration_status,
       coalesce(r.payment_status, 'NONE') AS payment_status,
       coalesce(r.has_ai_counsellor, false) AS ai_counsellor,
       r.gender,
       r.mobile_number,
       r.created_at
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = r.program_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id DESC

functions.name: my_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: whether their own reports actually exist, checked against the stored report records. Returns the report number, whether the main report is generated and downloadable, when it was generated, their trait code and style, and separately whether the level 3 IAT report and the level 4 Metaphor report exist. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenToUse: is my report ready
what is my report number
can I download my report
do I have an IAT or metaphor report
whenNotToUse: Not for whether the assessment itself is finished — use my_assessment_status.
Not for producing a download link — that is generate_my_report.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id)
       s.id AS session_id,
       s.status AS session_status,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.session_id IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_ready,
       (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_downloadable,
       ar.generated_at AS main_report_generated_at,
       pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       (iat.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS iat_report_ready,
       (mr.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       CASE
         WHEN ar.session_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Report is ready'
         WHEN s.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN 'Assessment finished, report not generated yet'
         ELSE 'No report — the assessment is ' || lower(coalesce(s.status, 'not started'))
       END AS readiness
  FROM assessment_sessions s
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = s.program_id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_session_id AS session_id, x.report_number, x.report_url,
              x.generated_at, x.dominant_trait_id
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id
         FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE'
        ORDER BY x.id DESC LIMIT 1) iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id
         FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.id DESC LIMIT 1) mr ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY s.id DESC

functions.name: platform_assessment_overview
functions.description: Administrator platform-wide count of assessment sessions grouped by status (COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, EXPIRED, and so on), across every company and student. Use for a health-of-the-platform overview.
whenToUse: how many assessments have been completed across the platform
give me a platform-wide assessment breakdown
how many sessions are in progress overall
whenNotToUse: Not scoped to one company — for that use candidate_status_counts as that company.
Available to administrators only.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       count(DISTINCT s.id) AS sessions
  FROM assessment_sessions s
 GROUP BY coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION')
 ORDER BY sessions DESC

functions.name: platform_level_throughput
functions.description: Administrator view of how much assessment has been completed at each level over a recent window, across every company: completions, distinct people, average score where the level has one, and the average minutes taken. Use for platform health and capacity.
whenToUse: how many assessments were completed at each level this month
how long does level 2 take on average
platform throughput by level
how many people finished level 3 in the last 90 days
whenNotToUse: Not scoped to one company — for that use level_completion_funnel as that company.
Not for session status overall — that is platform_assessment_overview.
Available to administrators only.

days.description: How far back to look, in days. Defaults to 30.

functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       l.pattern_type AS measures,
       count(DISTINCT a.id) AS completed,
       count(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS people,
       round(avg(a.total_score), 1) AS average_score,
       round(avg(extract(epoch FROM a.completed_at - a.started_at) / 60), 1) AS average_minutes
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE a.status = 'COMPLETED'
   AND a.completed_at >= now() - make_interval(days => coalesce({{param:days}}::int, 30))
 GROUP BY l.level_number, l.name, l.pattern_type, l.sort_order
 ORDER BY l.sort_order

functions.name: program_report_breakdown
functions.description: Registered, completed and report-ready counts for each program — School Students, College Students, Employee, CXO and so on — largest program first. Shows where reports are outstanding.
whenToUse: report readiness by program
how many college students have reports
split completions by program
whenNotToUse: Not for a per-level split — that is level_report_coverage.
Not for a single overall total — that is report_readiness_summary.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
         r.id AS registration_id,
         coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
         s.id AS session_id, s.status
    FROM registrations r
    LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
    LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, s.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s.id DESC
)
SELECT latest.program,
       count(*) AS registered,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE latest.status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar
          WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = latest.session_id)) AS report_ready
  FROM latest
 GROUP BY latest.program
 ORDER BY registered DESC, latest.program

functions.name: report_readiness_summary
functions.description: One row of headline counts about reports: how many candidates are registered, how many finished the assessment, how many have a main report generated, how many of those are downloadable, how many have a level 3 IAT report, how many have a level 4 Metaphor report, and how many finished but still have no report. Counted from the stored report records, so it reflects what actually exists.
whenToUse: how many reports are ready
how many registered and how many completed the assessment
how many candidates are waiting on a report
report generation status overall
whenNotToUse: Not for a per-candidate answer — that is candidate_report_status.
Not for a per-program split — that is program_report_breakdown.
Not for a per-level split — that is level_report_coverage.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH reg AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id) r.id AS registration_id, s.id AS session_id, s.status
    FROM registrations r
    LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, s.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s.id DESC
)
SELECT count(*) AS registered_candidates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE reg.status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed_assessment,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id)) AS main_report_ready,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar
          WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id AND ar.report_url IS NOT NULL)) AS main_report_downloadable,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM iat_reports i
          WHERE i.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id AND i.status = 'DONE')) AS iat_report_ready,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM metaphor_reports mr WHERE mr.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id)) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE reg.status = 'COMPLETED' AND NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id)) AS completed_but_no_report
  FROM reg

functions.name: stalled_attempts
functions.description: Candidates in your company whose deadline for a level has already passed without them finishing it, most overdue first, with how many days ago the deadline was. These are the people who need a new window rather than a reminder.
whenToUse: who missed their deadline
who has run out of time
which assessments expired without being finished
who needs their assessment reopened
whenNotToUse: Not for deadlines still in the future — that is attempts_expiring_soon.
Not for a status breakdown — use candidate_status_counts.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       l.level_number,
       l.name AS level,
       a.status,
       coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) AS deadline_was,
       round(extract(epoch FROM now() - coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at)) / 86400) AS days_overdue
  FROM assessment_attempts a
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
  JOIN assessment_levels l ON l.id = a.assessment_level_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND a.status <> 'COMPLETED'
   AND coalesce(a.must_finish_by, a.expires_at) < now()
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY a.id, deadline_was

functions.name: trait_code_distribution
functions.description: How many candidates fall into each behavioural trait code — the two-letter DISC blend such as DI, CD, CS — with the style name that code means and each code's share of all reported candidates. Largest group first. Answers "how many are in the DI trait".
whenToUse: how many candidates are in the DI trait
breakdown by trait code
which personality styles are most common
distribution of DISC blends
whenNotToUse: Not for the names of the candidates in a code — that is candidates_by_trait_code.
Not for one candidate's style — that is candidate_behavioural_profile.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id) r.id AS registration_id, ar.dominant_trait_id
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
   WHERE ar.dominant_trait_id IS NOT NULL
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, ar.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, ar.id DESC
)
SELECT pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       count(*) AS candidates,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / nullif(sum(count(*)) OVER (), 0), 1) AS percent_of_reported
  FROM latest l
  JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = l.dominant_trait_id
 GROUP BY pt.code, pt.blended_style_name
 ORDER BY candidates DESC, trait_code
